All three voters agree, and I checked the cited code myself. Existence comes from the ActualSlowAxis.fromNatural instance of exists_local_slow_hierarchy. It gives one radius and one complex tube around [−1,1] for every n, which is stronger than the paper's order-dependent neighbourhoods. It also gives (5.2)–(5.6) on 0<X≤endpoint·e^δ, zero axis values for all five stored components, joint C^∞ profiles and η-holomorphy of every mixed jet. Uniqueness is positive_solution_unique for system (5.7), which matches the paper's own proof; it lives only in PaperAdditionalResults, off the main chain. stepRaw/stepComponent_profile ties that theorem to the hierarchy. Four residual differences, all low severity: the uniqueness class is stated for (5.7) rather than for profiles; the inner-collar placement of a is missing; the recursion takes uncut lower orders; and the generic theorem is vacuous when U = ∅.

findings.summary: Uniqueness is proved only for the six-component system (5.7) with complex η and all six components zero at the axis. Uniqueness for real-η profile solutions of (5.2)–(5.6) is not stated. The reduction is routine.

The paper feeds order n the finalized lower orders, with their cutoffs and moment corrections. The Lean hierarchy feeds it its own uncut inner lower orders, so on (X_keep, a²] it solves a different recursion. The per-order theorems accept any regular lower history.

The generic exists_local_slow_hierarchy does not require [−1,1] ⊂ U. With U = ∅ every LocalHierarchy field except `starts` is vacuous. The content comes from the ActualSlowAxis instance, where U contains a fixed tube around [−1,1].
